column5: It is a warm afternoon on a busy street by the sea.
The palm trees move in a soft breeze.
All of it, the warmth, the wind, the light on every wall, comes from one star.
Close your eyes and you can feel it on your skin.
Now imagine that, at this very second, it simply goes dark.
Sunlight takes eight minutes and twenty seconds to travel to Earth.
The light falling on this street right now left the Sun before it went out.
It is still on its way.
If you looked up, the Sun would still be there, exactly where it always is.
But it would be a ghost.
An image of a star that is no longer burning.
So for eight minutes, everything would look completely normal.
Nothing travels faster than light, so no warning could reach us any sooner.
But every second, the last of the sunlight is closer to running out.
And then, at eight minutes and twenty seconds,
And after it, there is no more.
It only ever shone with borrowed sunlight.
Above the street, the stars would come out in the middle of the afternoon.
